newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Plant, equipment contribute to Australia GDP.
newsitem.headline: Plant, equipment contribute to Australia GDP.

text.p: Plant and equipment investment will contribute 0.15 percentage points to September quarter growth in Australian GDP, statistics bureau figures show.

The positive contribution from plant and equipment compares with average expectations of a slightly negative or zero contribution from all business investment, of which plant and equipment is a component.

The bureau's Private New Capital Expenditure survey also gives an estimate for buildings and structures investment, but this element is not used directly in the gross domestic product data and has been misleading in the past.
Nonetheless, the buildings and structures data imply a detraction from quarterly growth of 0.07 percentage points.

The bureau has revised up its estimates for the previous three quarters. Total capital spending in the June quarter has been revised up by A$56 million, the March quarter by A$263 million and the December quarter by A$15 million.
However, the plant and equipment component has been revised down by A$384 million for June. An upward revision of A$442 million to buildings and structures offset this.
Buildings and structures, were largely responsible for the March revision since they were revised up A$230 million.
(All figures are in the constant 1989/90 values used in GDP data.)
